title: Localized augmented polynomial-resolution model
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S\subseteq R$ a multiplicative subset containing $1$, and $B=S^{-1}R$, with $0\in S$ allowed. Let $T$ be a commutative $R$-algebra and $P_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon}T$ a polynomial resolution in the sense of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Put $T_S=S^{-1}T$ and $Q_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_R B$, using scalar extension [def-weil-module-base-change], with augmentation $p\otimes b\mapsto(\epsilon(p)/1)b$. Then $Q_\bullet\to T_S$ is a polynomial resolution over $B$. More precisely, for every $R$-module $M$ there is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism $B\otimes_R M\cong S^{-1}M$ sending $(r/s)\otimes m$ to $rm/s$, with inverse $m/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes m$. These maps, with the tensor factors interchanged, identify the augmented alternating-face complex $s(Q_\bullet)\to T_S[0]$ with the termwise localized augmented complex $S^{-1}s(P_\bullet)\to S^{-1}T[0]$. For any polynomial coordinates $P_n=R[E_n]$, the coefficient map identifies $Q_n$ with $B[E_n]$, for arbitrary sets $E_n$. In particular, when $T=B$, the isomorphism $S^{-1}B\cong B$, $b/s\mapsto(s/1)^{-1}b$, makes this a polynomial resolution of $B$ over $B$, with augmentation $p\otimes b\mapsto\epsilon(p)b$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with its base and algebra both $R$, its first module $R$, its second module $M$, and multiplicative subset $S$. It gives $S^{-1}(R\otimes_RM)\cong B\otimes_RM$, $(r\otimes m)/s\mapsto(r/s)\otimes m$. The maps $R\otimes_RM\to M$, $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$, and $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ are inverse by the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Localizing these maps using [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] therefore gives an $R$-linear isomorphism $G_M:S^{-1}M\to B\otimes_RM$, $m/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes m$. It is $B$-linear: $G_M((a/t)(m/s))=(1/(ts))\otimes am=(a/t)((1/s)\otimes m)$. Its inverse $F_M$ sends $(r/s)\otimes m=(1/s)\otimes rm$ to $rm/s$. For any $R$-linear $h:M\to N$, both composites in $F_N(1\otimes h)=(S^{-1}h)F_M$ send $(r/s)\otimes m$ to $r h(m)/s$; pure tensors generate, so the equality holds. These are the claimed maps and their naturality.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), its explicit fraction formula and proof; Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule); Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).

proof.text: The switch $p\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes p$ and its inverse are linear maps by the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Consequently Step 1 gives $\alpha_M:M\otimes_RB\xrightarrow{\sim}S^{-1}M$, $m\otimes(r/s)\mapsto rm/s$. For an $R$-algebra $C$, it is an algebra isomorphism: $\alpha_C((c\otimes r/s)(c\prime\otimes r\prime/t))=rr\prime cc\prime/(st)=\alpha_C(c\otimes r/s)\alpha_C(c\prime\otimes r\prime/t)$, and it sends $1\otimes1$ to $1/1$. Here products on the tensor algebra are obtained by extending the multiplication of $C$ as in [def-weil-module-base-change]. Define the faces and degeneracies of $Q$ by $d_i\otimes1$ and $s_i\otimes1$. Scalar extension preserves compositions and identities, so every simplicial identity for $P$ remains an identity for $Q$. Naturality of $\alpha$ identifies these maps with $p/s\mapsto d_i(p)/s$ and $p/s\mapsto s_i(p)/s$. With $C=T$ the same naturality identifies the induced augmentation with $p\otimes b\mapsto(\epsilon(p)/1)b$, as required.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), bilinearity relations; Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), formula; localization functor immediately before Tag 00CS.

proof.text: Choose any coordinates $P_n\cong R[E_n]$ supplied by the polynomial-resolution hypothesis [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], applied to $R\to B$ and the set $E_n$, $B\otimes_RR[E_n]\cong B[E_n]$ via $b\otimes p\mapsto b\bar p$. Compose with the factor switch of Step 2. This gives $Q_n\cong B[E_n]$ with the asserted coefficient map and variable images. The cited statement allows an arbitrary set of variables; no finite generation or finiteness assumption is introduced.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof: u(P_bullet) = P_bullet tensor_A A_prime; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), polynomial terms. Polynomial scalar extension is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The underlying alternating-face complex is $s(P)^{-n}=P_n$, with differential the finite sum $\sum_i(-1)^id_i$, by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Write $d_n$ for this sum from degree $-n$ to degree $1-n$. The maps of Step 2 give $\alpha_{P_{n-1}}((d_n\otimes1)(p\otimes r/s))=r d_n(p)/s=(S^{-1}d_n)(\alpha_{P_n}(p\otimes r/s))$. Scalar extension is linear on maps [def-weil-module-base-change], hence the alternating sum on $Q$ is exactly $d_n\otimes1$. For the augmentation the corresponding equality is $\alpha_T((\epsilon\otimes1)(p\otimes r/s))=r\epsilon(p)/s$. Thus these degreewise inverse maps form an isomorphism of the augmented complexes, including their maps to $T_S[0]$. This is an actual isomorphism of complexes, not only an identification of their homology groups.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof: s(P_bullet) tensor_A A_prime = s(P_bullet tensor_A A_prime); Tag 08QI (remark-resolution).

proof.text: The polynomial-resolution hypothesis [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] says that $\cdots\to P_2\xrightarrow{d_2}P_1\xrightarrow{d_1}P_0\xrightarrow{\epsilon}T\to0$ is exact: the negative homology groups vanish, the induced map $P_0/\operatorname{im}d_1\to T$ is an isomorphism, and $\epsilon$ is surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] to each consecutive triple of this sequence, including $P_1\to P_0\to T$ and $P_0\to T\to0$. The localized augmented complex is exact. By Step 4 the augmentation $s(Q)\to T_S[0]$ is consequently a quasi-isomorphism. Each augmentation $Q_n\to T_S$ is surjective: for $t/s\in T_S$, choose $p\in P_n$ with $\epsilon(p)=t$ and use $p\otimes(1/s)$. Together with Step 3, this checks every clause of the definition of polynomial resolution over $B$.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), localized case of its resolution computation; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution). Exactness input: algebra.tex, Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact).

proof.text: Finally let $T=B$. Every $s\in S$ acts on $B$ by the invertible element $s/1$, with inverse $1/s$. Therefore $\psi:S^{-1}B\to B$, $b/s\mapsto(s/1)^{-1}b$, is well defined: a relation $u(tb-sc)=0$ becomes $tb=sc$ after multiplying by the inverse of $u/1$, and multiplying by the inverses of $s/1,t/1$ gives equal images. The fraction formulas [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] show additivity and $B$-linearity. The maps $\psi$ and $b\mapsto b/1$ are inverse, since $((s/1)^{-1}b)/1=b/s$. The same formulas show multiplicativity and preservation of $1$. Composing the augmentation of Step 2 with $\psi$ sends $p\otimes b$ to $\epsilon(p)b$, so Step 5 gives the last assertion. If $0\in S$, the fraction relation makes $B$, every $S^{-1}M$, and $T_S$ zero; $M\otimes_RB=0$ by the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. All the displayed maps and resolution conditions remain valid, and $B[E_n]$ is the zero ring even for empty or infinite $E_n$.
